Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Quick weekly sync on the Nimbus quantization pilot. Primary focus: explain last week's anomalous quality delta on INT8 blend, run FP8 ablation, triage a latency regression observed in the 8k context bench, and agree next steps for an on-prem VPC trial. Action: run longer-context regressions, share updated pricing, provision VPC test cluster.

Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcripts may contain errors):
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then Marcus will walk through the new runs. Hey Priya, can you hear us?
[00:05] Priya: Yep, all good, thanks. We got a packed list, mainly that INT8 drop we saw, and then the latency bump on the 8k suite.
[00:12] Marcus: cool, I'll share screen in a sec. Quick TL;DR: INT8 saved about 42% token cost on the 2k baseline but we saw a small quality delta on two of Nimbus' clinical prompts, about a 2.4 point drop in our internal QA metric. FP8 blends look promising but the latency tail increased slightly on long contexts, and we think that's due to extra dequant/requant steps when the KV cache grows.
[00:34] Daniel: yeah the 2.4 drop is noticeable for us on the triage prompts — it's mostly hallucination on table field mappings, not fluency per se. That's problematic.
[00:45] Marcus: Understood — so what we did this week, on the Redwood side: ran an INT8-only conversion, an FP8-mix strategy (calls it fp8-blend in the sheet), and FP16 baseline. We included KV cache stress for contexts at 4k, 8k, and 16k. The bench results are in the shared sheet. Quick numbers: INT8 throughput improved 2.8x at 2k, average latency down ~110ms; FP8 gives ~2.3x throughput, latency similar to INT8 on short contexts but tail grows ~12-18ms at 8k+.
[01:18] Priya: do you have error bars or sample counts? I want to see N for the clinical prompts.
[01:23] Marcus: yes — N is 120 prompts per config for the clinical suite. For the long-context tests N is smaller (40) because each run is heavier.
[01:32] Aisha: on infra: when the KV increases we start seeing mem copies between CPU and GPU more often on the FP8 path — could that explain the latency tail?
[01:40] Marcus: possibility. FP8 execution on our runtime currently requires an extra quant/dequant on some attention kernels if the fused kernel for long-kv isn't selected. Kernel selection path might be falling back to a generic kernel when sequence-length > threshold. We're tracking that.
[01:55] Sofia: so two separate issues: a) the quality delta on certain templates in INT8 and b) latency tail on FP8/FP8-blend for long contexts. We need to prioritize stability for the clinical prompts.
[02:05] Priya: correct. Even a small regression on those prompts triggers internal risk flags because of downstream extraction to EHR fields.
[02:12] Tom: from procurement side, we're also watching the cost numbers; if INT8 reduces cost materially that's compelling but not if it breaks critical outputs.
[02:20] Marcus: Agreed. For the quality side we investigated quantization-aware calibration (calib) differences. We used per-channel minmax and a small representative corpus; seems some token embedding ranges for clinical jargon compress badly under symmetric int8. FP8 keeps more dynamic range and reduces those mis-maps.
[02:38] Daniel: can you run a per-layer sensitivity map? We had earlier requests but maybe not at layer granularity for our prompt set.
[02:45] Marcus: We have per-block sensitivity in the bench (sheet tab: layer-sens) but not the per-token heatmap. Can run a focused per-layer ablation on the top-5 suspect blocks. That should point to whether it's embedding layer vs middle-layers.
[02:58] Priya: please do. If it's the embeddings then we may consider hybrid approach: keep embeddings in fp16, rest int8.
[03:06] Marcus: that's a logical path. We can do embedding-fp16 + rest-int8 and try. We already have a prototype conversion for mixed precision.
[03:13] Leah: note for the pilot contract: we also want an explicit rollback clause in case quality dips on the gold prompts. Sofia will handle that.
[03:20] Sofia: yep I'll update the addendum.
[03:23] Marcus: on the latency front: Aisha, do you have perf counters or logs showing GPU mem spikes around the tail events?
[03:30] Aisha: I pulled dmesg and nvidia-smi sampling; memory didn't saturate but we saw periodic copy stalls and a few kernel timeouts — not full OOM though. Could be sync points when the kernel selection switches.
[03:40] Marcus: that sync might be the dequant step I mentioned — if the runtime picks a non-fused kernel for >8k seq, it does an intermediate dequant which forces a barrier. We'll try to force the fused kernel for the FP8 path and re-run.
[03:51] Daniel: is forcing a fused kernel safe across model revisions? We will have model version pins, but we also expect small param delta.
[03:58] Marcus: safe-ish; the fused kernel has preconditions (attention layout, kv stride). We need to validate across a few model checkpoints. That is in today's worklist.
[04:06] Priya: What's the expected delta if we can force fused kernel?
[04:09] Marcus: preliminary estimate: tail latency drop by ~10-15ms, throughput similar. It should remove the jitter.
[04:16] Sofia: procurement question — what's the cost delta if we move to FP8 blend rather than INT8?
[04:21] Marcus: FP8 is slightly higher unit cost since throughput is not quite as good as INT8; rough estimate per million tokens: INT8 $X vs FP8 $X+15%. But if FP8 reduces rework or manual triage it's often worth it. We'll put exact numbers in the sheet.
[04:36] Tom: would be helpful to see modeled TCO across our volume profile.
[04:40] Sofia: we will deliver a TCO spreadsheet with sensitivity to throughput and latency SLOs.
[04:45] Priya: about regression checks — Marcus, can you run the clinical gold prompts in a more adversarial pass? We want to throw edge-case field names and truncated notes.
[04:55] Marcus: yes, we'll expand the suite to include edge cases and also run a token-level diff to isolate where hallucination triggers.
[05:03] Ravi: I've got a question on privacy & KMS — if we do a VPC/on-prem test, can we bring our own KMS so keys never leave Nimbus?
[05:10] Aisha: that's a requirement for us, yes.
[05:13] Marcus: Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS). For the hosted pilot we used a Redwood-managed KMS, but for the on-prem VPC trial we can set up BYOK. Marcus: will coordinate with infra docs.
[05:24] Priya: timeline — we want to decide on whether to scale the pilot next week based on these triage results. Can we commit to a decision call?
[05:31] Sofia: let's do a follow-up on Friday next week (2026-02-27) after Marcus runs the ablation and Aisha provisions the VPC.
[05:38] Daniel: fine. Also we had one more oddity: in one run INT8 looked better on rouge than fp16 on a free-text task — is that plausible or mis-logged?
[05:47] Marcus: that may be an artifact: sampling seeds differ and we didn't fix the RNG across variants for that run. We'll re-run with fixed seeds to compare apples-to-apples.
[05:56] Priya: good call.
[06:00] Sofia: okay let's recap next steps: Marcus does per-layer ablation and hybrid embedding-fp16 test, re-run long-context with forced fused kernel for FP8, fix RNG and re-run the one odd rouge case, Leah and Sofia update pilot contract, Aisha sets up VPC testbed, Ravi confirms KMS/residency constraints.
[06:18] Tom: procurement will wait for the updated pricing and contract before sign-off.
[06:22] Marcus: timing on runs — per-layer ablation ~24-36 hours, long-context kernel forcing bench ~12 hours, full regression suite ~48 hours depending on queue. Will push results to the sheet as they land.
[06:35] Daniel: please mark any runs where we see >1% quality delta on gold prompts as P0.
[06:40] Priya: agreed.
[06:42] Sofia: any other blockers?
[06:43] Priya: none from my side.
[06:44] Aisha: will need credentials for the test cluster; sending to Leah out-of-band.
[06:49] Leah: got it.
[06:50] Sofia: thanks everyone. We'll reconvene 2026-02-27 same time. I'll send calendar invite.
[06:55] (meeting ends)
